cands.bio: Democrat who has represented Alabama House District 58 (Birmingham area) since winning a 2017 special election, succeeding Oliver Robinson. Born and raised in Birmingham. Holds an accounting degree from Tuskegee University and worked as a real estate broker.

controversies.text: Hollis was arrested Sept. 22, 2019, at a Destin, Florida hotel on a misdemeanor battery charge. A witness told police she shoved a male family member. Hollis and the man denied any altercation, though she admitted throwing a glass. She was released the next morning on a signature bond. No court outcome was found.

cands.gaps: We found no stated positions from Hollis on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, guns, school choice or police funding. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2022 or 2026 candidate surveys. Her Ballotpedia list of sponsored bills was empty in the page we read, so we could not review her bills. We found no record of any endorsements. We found no foreign ties. We could not find what came of the 2019 arrest. We did not find when her career as a real estate broker began or ended, or any other work history.

pro-life.evidence: Introduced HB 238 in 2020, a bill requiring vasectomy for men after a third child or before age 50. Hollis said it would "neutralize" the Alabama Human Life Protection Act, which restricts abortion.
